HOW WE TEACH

Close reading.
Open minds.

An approach to English that values the quality of a thought and the care with which it is expressed.

I.

Understand
before you label.

Identifying a technique is useful when it helps explain a writer’s meaning. We focus on the connection between a specific detail, its effect and the wider purpose of a text.

II.

Give evidence
a purpose.

A well-chosen reference should move an argument forward. Literature study asks students to connect their interpretation to what the text actually says and how it is written.

III.

Write clearly.
Think deliberately.

In Language, clarity comes from selecting the right ideas and organising them for the task. In Literature, it comes from a focused argument and precise textual support.
